## Command Details

```text
Register controlled Runners, their closed operation capabilities, and governed
execution requests (F052). A Runner is an EXTERNAL executor identity: id, version,
integrity digest, owner, and closed capabilities (declared effects, path scope
shape, timeout bound, credential requirement, rollback declaration) — never
command text, and Amber never spawns anything (ADR-0022). Registration is a
human-approved governance mutation binding a single-use committed human Decision;
unknown runner, version drift, and integrity mismatch fail closed. A request is
the closed declaration of one intended execution: risk derives from capability
facts through a versioned pinned policy (callers carry no risk field), semantic
refusals are recorded as immutable denied events, and authorization consumes a
single-use F050 Approval whose subject binds exactly one requestHash and
environment (runner-request:<environment>:<requestHash>). Versioned environment
profiles gate admission: development requires an isolated scope, staging admits
allowlisted deploy/rollback only with rollback rehearsal Evidence, production
grants preparation/diagnosis/runbook.* only; credentials are opaque short-lived
handles (never secret values), and the rehearsing party cannot approve its own
rehearsal. Execution settles durably: prepare binds one registered executor to
one authorized request, the external Runner submits one result receipt, and
Amber derives the outcome (attempted|timed-out|failed|committed|rolled-back) —
non-zero exit, signal, timeout, and scope escape fail explicitly, and sandbox
assurance, credential assurance, and result integrity stay separate fields.

Subcommands:
  register --id <id> --runner-version <v> --integrity <sha256:...>
        --runner-owner <owner> --decision-identity <identity> --revision <n>
  capability --id <runner-id> --runner-version <v> --capability <name>
        --capability-version <v>

        --timeout-ms <n> --credential <none|scoped> --rollback <declaration>
        --decision-identity <identity> --revision <n>
  request --id <runner-id> --runner-version <v> --capability <name>
```

## Boundaries & Safety

- `--target <path>` selects repository state. Amber confines these target-relative paths, refusing `..` and symlink escapes before reading or writing: plan and scaffold destinations (including `accept --plan`), memory and context payloads, harness inputs, adapter allow-lists, workflow reports and their output directory, ledger exports, execution readiness plans, session and worktree state, governance report output, wiki export and handoff bundle output directories.
- Path validation is not OS sandboxing, and the confinement above covers only the surfaces it names, and a confined flag still accepts an absolute destination only when it stays inside the target. `governance audit --output`, `governance readiness --output`, `security audit --output`, `loop record --output`, and `explain --markdown` resolve against the working directory instead of `--target`. A path flag not listed here is confined only when the command that reads it routes through the boundary. A governed or verification command still runs with your user's file permissions.
- `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, `workflow assess` and `governance report` reject output destinations that resolve to the target root, including `.`, an absolute root path, `nested/..`, and symlink or junction aliases of the root. Output subdirectories and defaults are unchanged.
- `wiki export` and `handoff bundle` check all planned file destinations and their parent directories before the first write, including copied wiki pages and optional replay files. An existing child symlink or junction outside the target refuses the export without changing output files. Concurrent link replacement is not prevented.
- A planned output file that shares its bytes with another name — a hard link, or a link to one — is refused before the write by `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, `workflow assess --output-dir`, `governance report --output`, `ledger export --out`, `knowledge context-review-sample --output`, `gate --plan` and `accept --plan` (the plan file they edit in place), `handoff` (the `session-handoff.md` it overwrites) and `hooks install` (the `pre-commit` hook it overwrites), even when both names stay inside the target. A link to a single in-target file is still written through, so it replaces that file's bytes; `workflow assess` is the exception, because it confines its output file to the `--output-dir` and so refuses a link whose referent sits elsewhere in the target. Like the child-link check above, this is checked before the write, so a link swapped in during the write is not caught.
- `handoff validate --bundle-dir .` and `workflow assess --handoff-bundle-dir .` still accept root-level bundles as read-only inputs. Explicit handoff validation paths outside `--target` are refused.
- Writing governance state goes through two shared helpers — the in-place JSON writer and the append-only JSONL ledger append — and both refuse a leaf that shares its bytes with another name. That covers the `.amber/` writers built on them (context pages and Loadouts, audit and event ledgers) without each one repeating the check; a raw write outside those helpers is guarded only where its own surface names it above.
- **Fail-Closed Behavior**: Corrupt governance state or invalid schema parameters immediately halt execution with non-zero exit codes.
